title: You & Me
supportedClaims: People make costly mistakes when they copy financial behavior from someone who is playing a different game with different incentives and horizons.
A trader, founder, retiree, journalist, and long-term saver can all be reacting rationally to their own incentives while looking absurd to one another.
The practical move is to define your own scoreboard before borrowing advice, signals, or urgency from people whose goals do not match yours.
caution: Knowing your own game can become self-sealing if you use it to ignore legitimate evidence or criticism.
